raw_case_text:
A 26-year-old African American man with AIDS presented with complaints of pleuritic chest pain, exertional shortness of breath, and hemoptysis of 3-week duration. He reported 10-pound weight loss in 6 months, drenching night sweats, and fever. He denied tobacco use but admitted using marijuana in the past. He denied neurological, gastrointestinal, or dermatological symptoms and had no recent travel. He was being treated with dapsone and elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir but was poorly compliant.
Of note, he was admitted 3 months earlier for similar complaints and was diagnosed with atypical pneumonia. A CT scan of the chest done on that admission showed diffuse fine noncalcified nodular densities in both lungs and small to moderate bilateral axillary, mediastinal, and hilar adenopathy. Bronchoscopy was unrevealing for endobronchial lesions. Bronchoalveolar lavage was negative for Pneumocystis jirovecii, acid fast bacilli, or fungal infection.
On index presentation, he had bilateral axillary and supraclavicular lymphadenopathy with signs of right lower lung zone consolidation on chest examination. There were no lesions on the skin or mucosa. Complete blood count was significant for normocytic anemia and metabolic panel was within normal limits. Absolute CD4 cell count is of 102 cells mu/L (17%). A repeat CT scan of the chest showed significant worsening of fibronodular infiltrates with consolidation in the right middle and lower lobes and left upper and lower lobes with bilateral axillary, supraclavicular, mediastinal, and hilar lymphadenopathy (Figure 1). Subsequent bronchoscopy revealed erythematous lesions on the proximal and distal part of the trachea and right middle lobe (Figure 2). Left main stem had vascular markings with dilated veins. These findings were consistent with endobronchial KS. Transbronchial biopsy was done and pathology was positive for atypical spindle cell proliferation with slit-like vascular spaces, lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate, and extravasated red blood cells (Figure 3). Nuclear HHV8 immunostain was expressed in atypical cells consistent with Kaposi Sarcoma.
He was started on a different HAART regimen: abacavir/dolutegravir/lamivudine after consultation with the infectious disease team. The patient tolerated the new medication and was discharged with appropriate follow-up. However he was readmitted twice: once with Immune Reconstitution Syndrome and the second time with massive hemoptysis. He developed acute respiratory failure, which unfortunately led to his death.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 26-year-old African American man with AIDS presented with a 3-week history of pleuritic chest pain, exertional shortness of breath, and hemoptysis.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient, who had been hospitalized 3 months earlier for similar symptoms diagnosed as atypical pneumonia (with diffuse fine noncalcified pulmonary nodules and negative BAL for Pneumocystis jirovecii, AFB, and fungi), re-presented with 3 weeks of pleuritic chest pain, exertional dyspnea, and hemoptysis, accompanied by fever, drenching night sweats, and a 10-pound weight loss over 6 months. He was prescribed dapsone and elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir for HIV/AIDS but was poorly compliant.
subjective.past_medical_history: HIV/AIDS with medication noncompliance; hospitalized 3 months prior for presumed atypical pneumonia. Social history: Never smoked tobacco, past marijuana use, no recent travel.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for pleuritic chest pain, exertional dyspnea, hemoptysis, fever, drenching night sweats, and 10-pound weight loss; negative for neurological, gastrointestinal, or dermatological symptoms. Prescribed home medications (noncompliant) were dapsone and elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir.

objective.physical_examination: Bilateral axillary and supraclavicular lymphadenopathy; physical signs of right lower lung zone consolidation on chest examination; no mucocutaneous lesions.
objective.routine_investigations: Complete blood count and chemistry: Normocytic anemia with normal comprehensive metabolic panel.
objective.advanced_workup: Immunological status: Absolute CD4+ T-cell count 102 cells/μL (17%). Prior admission chest CT and bronchoscopy (3 months earlier): Diffuse fine noncalcified bilateral pulmonary nodules and bilateral axillary/mediastinal/hilar adenopathy; no endobronchial lesions; BAL negative for Pneumocystis jirovecii, acid-fast bacilli, and fungi. Index admission repeat chest CT: Marked progression of bilateral fibronodular infiltrates with consolidation in the right middle/lower lobes and left upper/lower lobes plus bilateral axillary, supraclavicular, mediastinal, and hilar lymphadenopathy. Index bronchoscopy and transbronchial lung biopsy: Erythematous endobronchial lesions in the proximal and distal trachea and right middle lobe with prominent dilated vascular markings in the left mainstem bronchus; transbronchial biopsy pathology demonstrated atypical spindle-cell proliferation with slit-like vascular spaces, lymphoplasmacytic infiltrates, extravasated erythrocytes, and positive nuclear HHV-8 immunostaining diagnostic of pulmonary Kaposi sarcoma.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Primary endobronchial and parenchymal pulmonary Kaposi sarcoma without mucocutaneous involvement in a patient with advanced HIV/AIDS (CD4 102 cells/μL), definitively confirmed by HHV-8-positive atypical spindle-cell proliferation on transbronchial lung biopsy (with Pneumocystis jirovecii, mycobacteria, and fungi excluded on BAL). Plan and clinical course: Antiretroviral therapy was switched to abacavir/dolutegravir/lamivudine, which he tolerated well at discharge; however, he required two subsequent readmissions—first for immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS) and second for massive hemoptysis and fatal acute respiratory failure.
